title: Separate finds the boxes in a dark window too, not just on a flat light page
goal: Right now, separating a screenshot of a whole app window gives you its words and none of its panels, toolbars or buttons, because the app only recognises a box when there is one flat colour behind everything. A person separating a capture of their own app expects the button they can see to come out as a button.
notes:

Three of five, including a capture of this app, return zero boxes. The cause is in the design doc (docs/design/separate-into-layers.md, The boxes, step 2): the page is the region holding most of the picture outer border, and if no one region holds half of it nothing is claimed at all. A window with a dark canvas, a toolbar and two panels has no such region, so the whole box pass gives up. Step 5 (something that fills the picture IS the picture) already descends one level; the fix is likely to let the sweep read a REGION of the picture against its own local background rather than demanding one page for the whole frame.
acceptance: A capture of a whole app window with a dark canvas, a toolbar and side panels gives back at least the panels and the buttons as their own layers
The five captures in queue/audits/2026-09-13-separate-whole-screenshot.json each report how many boxes come out, before and after
Nothing that is not a box starts coming out: the settings pane capture still gives exactly its two buttons
A playtest walk separates a whole-window capture and checks the boxes by name

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. The task notes point at one line and they are right about it, but reading the code is not reproducing it, so I ran the bench first and then instrumented the sweep over all six captures. Three separate gates were each enough on their own to return zero boxes, and fixing only the named one would have shipped a fix that still found almost nothing: (1) pageRegion demanded ONE colour region holding half the picture's outer border, and a window offers 31/17/13 percent; (2) even with a background found, the window and the desktop around it are ONE connected piece running off every side of the frame, and a piece the frame cut is thrown away BEFORE the 'something that fills the picture IS the picture' step can look inside it, so the whole window went in the bin; (3) what is left of a window's chrome once the canvas and the panels are cut out of it is a comb, too sparse to be a box and too big to be nothing, and it was dropped with every button on it. The shortest version that delivers the value is the same rule said three times: a thing is what interrupts a background, and scenery is looked THROUGH rather than handed back.

MEASURED, before and after, on six real captures plus two photographs. Boxes out: settings pane 10 then 10, encyclopedia page 11 then 11, dark inspector crop 0 then 3, browser dashboard 0 then 27, this app's whole screen 0 then 19, mountain photograph 0 then 0, second photograph 0 then 0. The two captures that already worked did not move by a single box, which is acceptance item 3 (its wording says 'exactly its two buttons', written before nesting landed; the settings pane has given 10 since then and still does).

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before calling it ready. Could not use the real app: the Mac's screen was locked for the whole task, so no walk runs and no picture can be taken. Judged on the rects instead, and they are real pointable things rather than noise - on the new window fixture the ten boxes are the title bar's panel button, the selected layer's row, the swatch on it, two checkboxes, two dropdowns, a control that came out as a real rounded rectangle, and the red rectangle on the artboard. What still feels wrong, all of it in the audit: the panels themselves never come out (deliberate - the chrome is what everything is sitting ON, and lifting it leaves a window-shaped hole with nothing behind it, so this went into the audit's evaluate list as a question rather than being decided quietly); the descent peels four layers of chrome and is still finding a piece covering half the picture when it hits its limit, so it stops because it is told to; and a 7.7 MP capture went from 92 ms to 502 ms to separate.

left rough: the box sweep now walks the whole picture up to four times on a capture it can keep peeling, and each pass is a full union-find over every pixel. That is where the 5x came from. Not filed: it is the honest cost of reading a window rather than a defect, it is off the main thread, and the worst real case measured is 502 ms.

Inherited the 05:18 runner's uncommitted files and ran the full suite, which it never got to. ONE real regression in them: aCardLeftInThePictureKeepsWhatWasSittingOnIt fails. A card the frame cut in half with a row on it used to give back nothing; the new scenery rule (big and full of holes) reads the card as background, so the row now comes out. Judged an improvement rather than a break - the old rule's reason was that lifting the row leaves a hole nobody can fill, and once the card is background the repair fills it with the card's own colour. Rewriting the test to assert BOTH: the row comes out, and the space it leaves reads white (the card) rather than the page. Design doc step 4 updated with the exception.

VERIFIED the rewrite, not assumed. Scripts/test.sh --filter 'SeparateIntoLayers|AppWindowSeparate|BoxSweep': 75 tests in 5 suites passed. The claim I made about the repair is measured rather than argued - the test prints 'PATCH the row's space on the cut card reads within 0/255 of the card', so lifting the row off a card the frame cut leaves the card's own white behind it and not a hole. Full suite before the rewrite: 7589 tests, 607 suites, that one test the only failure.

MEASURED BEFORE AND AFTER MYSELF, same machine, same release build, by stashing Sources/PhotonzCore/BoxSweep.swift and running the bench twice. Boxes out, before -> after: settings pane 10 -> 10, encyclopedia page 11 -> 11, dark inspector crop 0 -> 3, browser dashboard 0 -> 27, this app's whole screen 0 -> 19, mountain photograph 0 -> 0, second photograph 0 -> 0. That is acceptance item 2 for all five named captures plus two photographs, and acceptance item 3: the two captures that already worked did not move by a single box. Separating time, before -> after: 7.7 MP whole screen 88 -> 478 ms, 5.1 MP dashboard 66 -> 185, 5.1 MP encyclopedia 130 -> 130, 1.4 MP settings pane 156 -> 156, 6.6 MP photograph 88 -> 73. The cost lands only on captures it can now actually read, which is the trade.
